newsitem.title: FRANCE: French cattle breeders block roads over mad cows.
newsitem.headline: French cattle breeders block roads over mad cows.

text.p: Cattle breeders blocked roads in several areas of central France on Friday to press demands for government aid in the face of dropping meat prices resulting from fears of mad cow disease, union sources said.
Roads, and several railway lines, were blocked by demonstrators across the Limousin, Auvergne and Burgundy regions, the sources said.
Police were not immediately available for comment.
Farmers unions leaders say meat sales have dropped by up to 25 percent as a result of fears of mad cow disease.
The unions want government subsidies to help carry them over what they hope is a passing crisis.

But British scientists said this week they had found more evidence that mad cow disease could spread to people. Their research published on Wednesday found a new variant of fatal Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD) in humans left traces very similar to brain-wasting mad cow disease -- bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE).
